bull_bear.body:
- Competitive environment / bidding pressure — The construction industry remains highly competitive, with several organised and unorganised contractors competing for projects; competitive bidding may place pressure on margins.
- Regulatory and approval risk — Construction projects are subject to various statutory approvals, permits, environmental requirements and other regulatory compliances; delays in obtaining approvals may affect project schedules and costs.
- Input cost inflation — Fluctuations in the prices of cement, steel, fuel, labour and other construction materials may adversely affect project margins, particularly where contracts do not provide adequate price-escalation protection.
- Working capital and receivables risk — Construction projects generally require significant working capital and timely collection of receivables; delays in certification or payments may affect liquidity.
- Availability of skilled manpower — The construction industry is dependent on skilled and semi-skilled manpower; shortages or higher labour costs may affect project execution.
- Project execution risk — Delays arising from weather conditions, site conditions, availability of materials, labour, approvals or changes in project scope can affect project schedules and profitability.
- Natural disasters and severe weather — The construction business is vulnerable to severe weather conditions and natural disasters such as hurricanes, floods, earthquakes, wildfires and droughts.
- Single-segment concentration — The Company deals in only one reportable segment, Construction, concentrating business risk in a single activity line.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

outlook.body:
- Outlook for the Indian construction and infrastructure sector remains positive, supported by India's economic growth, increasing urbanisation, infrastructure development, public capital expenditure and private-sector investment
- Government's continued focus on infrastructure development, roads, bridges, railways, urban infrastructure, housing and water supply is expected to support demand for construction services
- Rapid urbanisation and expansion of cities are expected to increase demand for residential, commercial, industrial and public infrastructure
- Increasing formalisation of the construction and real estate sectors is expected to favour organised contractors with established execution capabilities, compliance systems and financial discipline
- Technology-enabled project management, digital monitoring, construction planning and automation can enhance productivity, project visibility and cost control
- Management remains cautiously optimistic about long-term prospects while recognising risks from competition, input costs, project execution and working-capital requirements
- The Company remains focused on timely project execution, quality of work, customer satisfaction and maintaining a sustainable order pipeline
